params.body:
## Why

Two things Shane decided on 18 September, after Ilse reported that "herhaal paswoord" showed no field:

1. An administrator typed the password of someone else. That password passed through him, nothing said whether the person ever got in, and the whole creation of a user hung on two fields that had quietly disappeared from the HTML for five days.
2. A user without the right to manage users could not change his own name or password at all; "Mijn profiel" opened the administrator's user modal ("gebruiker Shane Deconinck", roles, API token), which is a screen about someone else.

Shane, on whether a staff member without an e-mail address could still get a password from his manager: "dan geen paswoord meer via personeelslid". So there is no exception, and an e-mail address is required.

## Invitation instead of a password (R P2-2.12, R P2-2.13, R P2-2.14)

- The user form has no password fields any more, on the create page, the create modal and the edit modal. Creating a user makes an account without a password and mails an invitation.
- The mail carries a signed link, valid seven days and usable once, in the language of the invited user. The user picks his own password (at least eight characters) and is signed in straight after; only the sha256 of the token is stored, so reading the database does not open an account.
- "Uitnodiging opnieuw sturen" (also the way for a forgotten password from the administration) sends the same mail and invalidates the previous link. Next to the button the modal says whether an invitation is open ("Uitgenodigd op ...") or since when the user is in.
- A garage administrator does this for his own people; across garages only a platform administrator.
- The button carries `data-invite-url` and one delegated listener handles it (`resources/js/invitations.js`): no global, no inline handler, so it also works inside a modal loaded over AJAX. The old `custom.passwordReset()` is gone.

## Own details on "Mijn profiel" (R P2-3.20)

- Every user, whatever his rights, edits his own first name, last name, e-mail address, phone, WhatsApp number and language there, and changes his own password (current one first, other devices signed out).
- Role, garage and the purchase-price right are shown as text: they belong to the administrator screens. A role or dealer sent along with the form is ignored.
- The page is wider (`max-w-5xl`), so the cards line up with the rest of the app.

## Tests

New: `UserInvitationTest` (6: hash only, the link works once and signs in, expired link changes nothing, sending again invalidates the old one, no password field in the form, no code writes a password from the user screens) and `ProfileOwnDetailsTest` (5: a user without rights sees and opens his own details, saves his name but not his role or dealer, cannot take an address that is taken, changes his password only with the current one, a guest gets nowhere). `UserPasswordFieldsTest` rewritten for the new reality, including "a password in the request is ignored" and "an address that is not an address is refused"; `TwoFactorTest` updated (own details are everyone's now). `SmokeTest` lists the guest invitation route with its reason.

Run: `UserInvitationTest|ProfileOwnDetailsTest|UserPasswordFieldsTest|TwoFactorTest|PasskeyRoutesTest|UserModalSaveTest|DelegationTest|LoginRememberTest|AlpineExpression|HandlerWiring|StylesheetSyntax|CompiledViews|LanguageParity|BuildContract|Rules*|FeatureFlagsScreen|SmokeTest`: **381 tests, 1860 assertions**, one pre-existing incomplete. `php bin/rules-sources`: Geen problemen. `npm run build`: green.

## After the merge

Nothing to set. The `user_invitations` table comes with the deploy migration. Mail goes out in production only (`Outbound::seal()` sends it to the log everywhere else), so an invitation on preview never reaches a dealer.

## Not in this PR

The user list column "uitgenodigd / actief" (the state is in the edit modal for now), and an administrator screen to invite someone who lost every device.
params.title: Invitation instead of a password typed by an administrator, and own details on the profile
